fields.features_heading: The Parts That Make the Answers Usable
fields.features_subheading: The first three decide who answers and how. The last three are for your team, once responses start to arrive.
fields.feature_1:
A screener that ends the survey early

Emergent builds the screener and its logic from your prompt. Anyone who has never hired a dog walker gets a short thank-you screen after question 1 and counts as screened out.
fields.feature_2:
Quotas that close a full segment

Set a number for each segment, such as 150 renters and 150 homeowners. Once a group reaches its number, the app stops taking its answers and the other group stays open.
fields.feature_3:
Phone-first, one question at a time

A link opened on a phone shows one question per screen, with a bar that counts what is left. The layout suits a QR code on a booth sign or a link sent by text message.
fields.feature_4:
Every result split by segment

Ask for the segment as a pick list, and the dashboard shows each question by segment beside the total. A feature that looks lukewarm overall can be one group's first choice.
fields.feature_5:
Responses in a database you own

Each response is a row in a database that belongs to you, segment and date included. The app can send qualified respondents to HubSpot, or any tool with an API, for interviews.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the full survey app to your GitHub repository, with the screener logic and the dashboard. Anyone on the team can read it or reuse it later.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams With a Product Call to Make
fields.tab_content_1:
For 224 of 612 people, the survey ends at the screener

Tallgrass Coffee wants to know whether cold-brew drinkers would sign up for a monthly subscription. Question 1 asks how often each person buys cold brew. Of the 612 people who start, 224 buy it less than once a month and see a thank-you screen. The other 388 go on to the subscription questions.
fields.tab_content_2:
Same-day delivery gets a yes from 212 dog owners

Brightwell Pet Supply asks 940 loyalty members whether they would order pet food for same-day delivery, and the dashboard splits the answers by pet. Dog owners say yes 212 of 517 times, against 66 of 298 cat owners. The same-day pilot starts with dog food.
fields.tab_content_3:
By day 3, the solo-firm quota of 100 is full

Lantern Ledger, a bookkeeping app, needs 100 accountants from each of 3 firm sizes before it picks which plan to build first. Solo firms fill their 100 on day 3. The app closes that group to new answers and sends product manager Odalys Brennan a Slack message, while the other two groups keep collecting.
fields.tab_content_4:
On question 5, dishwasher-safe leads with 87

At its trade show booth, Marlow Kitchenware hangs a QR code that opens a short survey on visitors' phones, one question per screen. On question 5 of 6, the skillet feature that matters most, dishwasher-safe leads with 87 of 214 answers. A lifetime warranty follows at 71.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Market Research Survey
fields.howto_description: Follow these steps to build a market research survey, reach only people in your market, and read the answers by segment.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the product call the survey will settle, such as whether to launch the subscription or which plan to build first. Every question should move that call. Anything that is only nice to know waits for a later study.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Type the survey in plain English: who should answer, who should be screened out, and what the results page shows. Emergent builds the survey, its database, and the dashboard from that prompt. Ask for any change in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put one or two screener questions first, and ask what people did in the past month instead of what they intend. Decide which answers end the survey before you write the rest. Word the screener so nobody can guess the answer that qualifies.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the segments you will compare, such as firm size or pet type, and set a number of answers for each. Make the segment question a fixed list of choices, so the quota count and the dashboard split read from one field.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the link to 10 people in your market who did not help write it, at least half of them on a phone. Time how long each one takes, and rewrite any question that two people read differently.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Publish the survey on its own link or on a custom domain (built into Emergent, uses credits). Then send it where your market already is: a customer email list, a QR code at a booth, or a link in a community newsletter.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Close it and read by segment
fields.howto_step_7_des: Close the survey once every quota is full. Read each question by segment before you look at the totals, and write down the decision next to the numbers that drove it.

faq_plan.q: What are paid market research surveys, and when should you pay students to take one?
faq_plan.ref: what are paid market research surveys for students
faq_plan.a: They are market research surveys that reward each person who finishes, with cash or a gift card. Pay students when they are the market you are studying, with a modest reward that is the same for everyone. Promise it only after the screener, and add one attention check to catch anyone clicking through for the reward.

faq_plan.q: How do you create a market research survey?
faq_plan.ref: how to create a market research survey
faq_plan.a: Write a short prompt for Emergent's AI survey builder that names the decision, who qualifies, and the segments to compare. Emergent turns that description into a working market research survey with a results page. The prompt chips on this page add a screener or segment quotas to it, and every later change is one more sentence.

faq_plan.q: Who should a customer research survey go to?
faq_plan.a: Send it to people who already buy from you, drawn from your own customer list, not a panel. Pick the group that matches the decision: recent buyers for a checkout question, or customers who left for a churn question. To hear from people who have never bought from you, run a market research survey with a screener instead.

faq_plan.q: In what order should market research survey questions go?
faq_plan.a: Put the screener first, then questions about what people do now, then the questions the decision rests on, with demographics last. Questions about gaps in a program you already run belong in a needs assessment survey, not here. Asking about behavior before opinion puts each opinion next to what that person did.

faq_plan.q: When should you hire market research survey companies?
faq_plan.a: Hire one when you cannot reach the people you need on your own, such as buyers in a narrow industry, or when you want a firm to run the whole study. Build it yourself when a customer list or a booth already puts you in front of your market. A survey built on Emergent has no response caps, however many people answer.

faq_plan.q: What are some market research survey examples?
faq_plan.a: A bakery can ask nearby offices whether they would order catered breakfasts on Fridays. A fitness app can ask lapsed users which missing feature would bring them back, and a furniture maker can ask renters how big their living rooms are before designing a smaller sofa. Each one starts from a single decision and screens for the people who face it.

faq_plan.q: How short should online market research surveys be?
faq_plan.a: Short enough that a person finishes in under 5 minutes on a phone, which means about 12 questions at most. Time yourself on a phone during the pilot and cut questions until you get there. Emergent can build the survey as a conversational flow, with one question per screen.

faq_plan.q: What should a customer needs survey ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with the job the customer is trying to get done and how they handle it today. Then ask them to rank the problems you could solve: the ranking shows which one matters most, not only which ones exist. Save your own product ideas for the end, after people have described the problem in their own words.

faq_plan.q: Which customer research survey questions give answers you can act on?
faq_plan.a: Questions about a specific recent event give the answers you can act on. 'The last time you reordered, what made you pick this store?' tells you more than 'Do you like the service?' Ask for a number or a choice where you can, and keep one open box for the reason behind it.

faq_plan.q: How do you conduct a market research survey once it is built?
faq_plan.ref: how to conduct market research survey
faq_plan.a: Recruit where your market already gathers, open the survey, and check each quota count daily, not only the total. After launch, a customer feedback survey to the people who buy tests whether the research held up. Meanwhile, the app can email one reminder to people on your list who have not answered and post a Slack alert when a segment fills.

plan.angle: The top 10 is guides (SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics, SBA, GWI, Attest, Investopedia) that explain what a market research survey is, plus survey-tool template pages; none shows a founder or product team building the survey a decision needs. This page is for that team: a screener that ends the survey for people outside the market, quotas that close a segment once it is full, results split by segment, a phone-first layout for in-person fieldwork, and every response in a database the team owns. The FAQ answers the builder's questions (incentives, question order, when to hire a firm, how to run it) as plain advice.
